name: dastHighSeverityIssuesCount
definition: The number of high-severity issues across the scan targets of a DAST product, each target counted from its most recent successful scan.
population: every scan target with a successful scan in a complete read of the successful-scan list (fewer than the 100 scans one read returns); the value is the sum of issue_counts.high.total over each target's newest successful scan
evidenceRequiredForTrue: A complete read (fewer than 100 successful scans, no GraphQL errors) in which every scan has status succeeded, a scan target id, a readable end time and an integer issue_counts.high.total; 0 only when every target's newest successful scan reports 0. An empty list or a full page is not measured.

openDecisions.question: Should another DAST product (for example a different web application scanner) be allowed to answer this key, or should it stay with Burp Suite DAST until a second implementation is replayed?
positions: any (registered): every Application Security integration may answer it, held to this definition.
listed: only Burp Suite DAST until a second product's implementation is replayed against real data.

citations: safeguards/devsecops/burpsuitedast/dasthighseverityissuescount.py (reads Integration-Service method listCompletedScans: scans { status end_time scan_target { id } issue_counts { high { total } } })
https://portswigger.net/burp/extensibility/dast/graphql-api/issuecounts.html (high: the number of high-severity issues found, by confidence; retrieved 2026-11-13)

changeLog.change: Registered for the PortSwigger Burp Suite DAST checks. No live server read yet, so the key is proposed and V0.

notes: Burp's severities are high, medium, low and info; there is no critical. Whether issue_counts leaves out issues marked false positive or accepted risk is not documented (UNVERIFIED).
